nobox.final_span:
Return on Social Investment. For CG Nepi, part of the challenge lies in not only finding a method to measure Return on Social Investment but also in utilizing it to demonstrate successes aligned with the expectations of the various tribes they rely on.
If a social enterprise collapses, it might offer a healthy and rewarding experience to the entrepreneurs involved, yet the social assets accumulated during the enterprise’s lifetime could still exist, provided they can be transferred in some form. The key asset here resides in the intellectual capital and common sense of solid three to four year old businesses.
